mechanism_narrative: The observed recovery in RETAIL_REC mobility over the last two weeks, moving from a low of -41.9% to -34.1%, indicates a sustained upward trend that will continue to drive retail and recreation activity higher over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: If the mean RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days is lower than -34.1%, this hypothesis is falsified.

mechanism_narrative: A significant week-on-week decrease in RESIDENTIAL mobility, indicating fewer people staying home, will directly translate to increased out-of-home activities, boosting RETAIL_REC over the next two weeks.
candidate_trigger: RESIDENTIAL falls by more than 1.5 points week-on-week
failure_condition: If RETAIL_REC does not increase over the next two weeks following a week-on-week drop in RESIDENTIAL mobility greater than 1.5 points, the hypothesis is false.

mechanism_narrative: The concurrent recovery in WORKPLACES and TRANSIT mobility, observed over the last two weeks, suggests a return to office-based work and associated commuting, which will synergistically increase RETAIL_REC as people frequent shops and restaurants near their workplaces or transit hubs over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: If RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days does not increase despite both WORKPLACES and TRANSIT showing a sustained recovery trend, this hypothesis is falsified.

mechanism_narrative: As weather improves, indicated by the recovery in PARKS mobility from -38.4% to -31.3% over the last two weeks, people will spend more time outdoors, leading to increased foot traffic in retail and recreation areas over the next week. This mechanism is particularly strong during warmer seasons.
candidate_trigger: PARKS mobility shows a week-on-week increase
failure_condition: If RETAIL_REC does not increase in the next week, despite a week-on-week increase in PARKS mobility during a period of generally improving weather, this hypothesis is false.

mechanism_narrative: The consistent positive baseline and recent increase in GROCERY_PHARM mobility suggests a stable level of essential outings. This stability provides a foundation for discretionary spending to recover, indirectly supporting an increase in RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: If RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days decreases while GROCERY_PHARM mobility remains stable or increases, this hypothesis is falsified.

mechanism_narrative: An acceleration in the recovery of WORKPLACES mobility, specifically if it surpasses a certain threshold of improvement, will signal a broader return to pre-pandemic routines, directly boosting RETAIL_REC over the next two weeks as more people commute and engage in out-of-office activities.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES mobility increases by more than 2 points week-on-week
failure_condition: If RETAIL_REC does not show an increase over the next two weeks following a week-on-week rise in WORKPLACES mobility exceeding 2 points, the hypothesis is false.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decrease in RESIDENTIAL mobility coupled with a concurrent increase in RETAIL_REC mobility indicates a shift in population behavior towards spending less time at home and more time in public spaces, driving further increases in retail and recreation activity over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: If RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days decreases while RESIDENTIAL mobility also decreases, or if RETAIL_REC increases while RESIDENTIAL mobility increases, this hypothesis is falsified.

mechanism_narrative: If local public health policies are perceived to be easing, the observed recovery in TRANSIT mobility from -39.3% to -33.9% will continue, facilitating greater access to retail and recreation venues and thereby increasing RETAIL_REC over the next two weeks. This mechanism is contingent on policy stability or easing.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT mobility shows a sustained week-on-week increase
failure_condition: If RETAIL_REC does not increase over the next two weeks despite a sustained increase in TRANSIT mobility, and no new public health restrictions are announced, this hypothesis is false.
